2026 IRS Schedule-C Tax Deductions Checklist for Etsy, Shopify & Amazon Sellers

Stop overpaying US self-employment tax on gross 1099-K numbers. Review the top 10 legal IRS Schedule-C business write-offs every US e-commerce seller must track.

1. Why Your 1099-K Shows More Money Than You Actually Received

Marketplaces like Etsy, Amazon, eBay, TikTok Shop, and Shopify Payments issue Form 1099-K reporting GROSS unadjusted sales—meaning they include refunded orders, buyer-paid shipping, and marketplace fees that never hit your bank account.

You only owe federal income tax and 15.3% self-employment tax on your NET profit (Schedule C Line 31). Failing to document fees and expenses means paying 25%–35% tax on money you never kept.

2. Top 8 Overlooked Schedule-C Write-Offs for Online Sellers

1) Raw materials, blank inventory & landed freight/import duties. 2) All marketplace listing, transaction, payment processing, and FBA/FBT fees. 3) Postage labels, poly mailers, boxes, thermal labels, and tape. 4) Paid ads (Etsy Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok GMV Max, Amazon PPC) and creator product samples.

5) SaaS & design tools (Shopify subscription, Printify Premium, Canva, Link My Books, QuickBooks). 6) Dedicated home office & inventory storage square footage. 7) Business internet/phone percentage & shipping printer hardware. 8) Professional education, CPA fees, and LLC/business license renewals.
